title: Quasi-coherent supported sections and their affine ideal-power description
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subset, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume the complementary open $X\setminus Z$ is retrocompact, meaning that its intersection with every affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact. Define the submodule sheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F$ by $\mathcal K(W)=\{s\in\mathcal F(W):s|_{W\setminus Z}=0\}$ for every open $W\subseteq X$. Then $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] there exists a finitely generated ideal $J\subseteq A$ with $Z\cap U=V(J)$, where $V(J)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $J$. For every such finitely generated defining ideal $J$, one has $\mathcal K(U)=\{m\in\mathcal F(U):J^n m=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$, where $J^n m=0$ means that every element of $J^n$ annihilates $m$.

proof.text: Put V=X\setminus Z and let j:V\hookrightarrow X be its open immersion. The assumed compactness of U\cap V for affine U is precisely the affine-open criterion for quasi-compactness of j. Restriction F|V is quasi-coherent; j is quasi-separated because it is an open immersion, so its direct image is quasi-coherent by the qcqs pushforward theorem. Take the actual categorical kernel K of the restriction-adjunction unit F -> j_*(F|V). The kernel theorem makes K quasi-coherent. The sectionwise kernel formula gives an injective inclusion into F on each W, whose image is exactly the kernel of F(W) -> F(W\cap V); the equality j(j^{-1}W)=W\cap V identifies its target with the one in the statement.

For an affine U, carry the compact open U\setminus Z along the affine isomorphism U ~= Spec Gamma(U,O_X). A compact open in a prime spectrum is the complement of V(J) for some finitely generated ideal J, by the basic-open basis and finite subcover argument. Lean uses the packaged Mathlib theorem PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_isOpen_iff_ideal. Pulling the equality back along the affine isomorphism gives x in Z iff J is contained in the prime corresponding to x. This works also for the empty open complement.

Fix any finitely generated defining ideal J on affine U and a supported section m. If a is in J, its basic open D(a) is contained in U\setminus Z, since every point of Z corresponds to a prime containing J. Thus m restricts to zero on D(a). Compactness of U and the compact-section power-torsion theorem give a^n m=0 for some n. Let I be the annihilator of the cyclic submodule generated by m. The preceding conclusion says J <= radical(I). The finitely generated radical-power lemma supplies N with J^N <= I; hence every element of J^N annihilates m. This uses the library radical-power lemma instead of a separate monomial calculation.

Conversely suppose J^N m=0. For every a in J, a^N belongs to J^N. Restrict this equality to D(a): the restricted a is a unit, hence its Nth power acts injectively, so m restricts to zero there. These basic opens cover U\setminus Z: at a point outside Z, its prime does not contain J, so some a in J is outside that prime. Sheaf uniqueness then gives m|_(U\setminus Z)=0. For N=0 the same unit calculation applies with a^0=1. If the complementary open is empty, the uniqueness argument applies to its empty cover. The image formula from the kernel construction converts this equivalence to the claimed range formula.

lean.statement: theorem exists_supportedSections_isQuasicoherent {X : Scheme.{u}} (Z : Closeds X) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (hretro : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → IsCompact ((U : Set X) ∩ (Z : Set X)ᶜ)) : ∃ (K : X.Modules) (ι : K ⟶ F), (∀ (W : X.Opens), Function.Injective (ι.app W) ∧ Set.range (ι.app W) = {s : Γ(F, W) | F.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W ⊓ ⟨(Z : Set X)ᶜ, Z.isClosed.isOpen_compl⟩ ≤ W)).op s = 0}) ∧ K.IsQuasicoherent ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U), (∃ (J : Ideal Γ(X, U)), J.FG ∧ ∀ (x : U), (x.1 ∈ Z ↔ J ≤ (hU.isoSpec.hom x).asIdeal)) ∧ (∀ (J : Ideal Γ(X, U)), J.FG → (∀ (x : U), (x.1 ∈ Z ↔ J ≤ (hU.isoSpec.hom x).asIdeal)) → ∀ (m : Γ(F, U)), m ∈ Set.range (ι.app U) ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ), ∀ (a : Γ(X, U)), a ∈ J ^ n → a • m = 0))
